<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="תשרי_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518914491_theRebbe_55" batchId="meluket-_D7_AA_D7_A9_D7_A8_D7_99_meluket__BH_POST_1766518914491_theRebbe_55__p002">
  <section v="3">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that all the festivals of Tishrei are characterized by the aspect of "one," beginning with Rosh Hashanah's unique mitzvah of shofar, which is a decree above reason, and continuing through Yom Kippur and Sukkos, where the unity of all Israel is emphasized in the mitzvos of the sukkah and the four species, especially the esrog.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">3)</t>
    <t s="1">And this can be understood based on what was stated above</t>
    <t s="2">(in the discourse beginning "In sukkos you shall dwell"10)</t>
    <t s="3">that all the festivals of the month of Tishrei are in the aspect of "one."</t>
    <t s="4">For, regarding Rosh Hashanah, our sages said,11</t>
    <t s="5">"The mitzvah of the day is with the shofar."</t>
    <t s="6">That is,</t>
    <t s="7">that what makes the day of Rosh Hashanah distinct from the other festivals is in one mitzvah</t>
    <t s="8">(a single and unique mitzvah),</t>
    <t s="9">the mitzvah of shofar.</t>
    <t s="10">And regarding this very mitzvah, the Rambam writes12</t>
    <t s="11">that it is a decree of the Scripture, above reason.</t>
    <t s="12">For although the mitzvah of shofar also alludes to the most exalted matters concerning repentance</t>
    <t s="13">(as the Rambam continues,12</t>
    <t s="14">"there is a hint in the matter," etc.),</t>
    <t s="15">nevertheless, its essence is a decree of the Scripture, above reason.</t>
    <t s="16">And similarly, this is also the case regarding Yom Kippur</t>
    <t s="17">[the conclusion of the ten days between Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur],</t>
    <t s="18">which is the aspect of "one" of all three aspects of world, year, and soul.</t>
    <t s="19">For the unique service of Yom Kippur is in the Holy of Holies, the aspect of "one" of world</t>
    <t s="20">(place),</t>
    <t s="21">on the day of Yom Kippur, which is called13</t>
    <t s="22">by the name "one in a year,"</t>
    <t s="23">the aspect of "one" of year</t>
    <t s="24">(time),</t>
    <t s="25">and is performed by the Kohen Gadol</t>
    <t s="26">[except that the Kohen Gadol does this as the agent of all Israel],</t>
    <t s="27">as it is written14</t>
    <t s="28">regarding him, "And Aharon was separated to sanctify him as holy of holies,"</t>
    <t s="29">the aspect of "one" of soul.</t>
    <t s="30">And similarly, this is also the case regarding Sukkos,</t>
    <t s="31">that in the matter of the sukkah</t>
    <t s="32">[for the mitzvah of dwelling in the sukkah is throughout all seven days of Sukkos,</t>
    <t s="33">from the first moment of their beginning]</t>
    <t s="34">the aspect of unity is emphasized</t>
    <t s="35">(the aspect of "one")</t>
    <t s="36">of all Israel, as our sages said,15</t>
    <t s="37">"All Israel are fit to dwell in one sukkah."</t>
    <t s="38">And likewise, this is also the case with the mitzvah of taking the four species</t>
    <t s="39">[whose purpose is to draw down the encompassing light</t>
    <t s="40">(of the one sukkah)</t>
    <t s="41">into the innerness16],</t>
    <t s="42">that in each of these four species, the aspect of unity is recognizable and emphasized,</t>
    <t s="43">and particularly in the esrog,</t>
    <t s="44">in which the aspect of unity is emphasized even more</t>
    <t s="45">[therefore, in the order of the four species in the verse17</t>
    <t s="46">(and the order in the Torah is also Torah)</t>
    <t s="47">the beginning is with the esrog, "the fruit of a beautiful tree"],</t>
    <t s="48">for that which the esrog is called in the verse "the fruit of a beautiful tree" is because it dwells on its tree from year to year,18</t>
    <t s="49">meaning that it endures the changes of the four seasons throughout the year,</t>
    <t s="50">to the extent that</t>
    <t s="51">(not only does it endure all the seasons, but)</t>
    <t s="52">it grows from them.</t>
    <t s="53">And from the aspect of unity in the esrog, this is also drawn into the other three species,</t>
    <t s="54">therefore, the concept of "beautiful" (hadar) in the three species is learned from the esrog.19</t>
    <t s="55">And in addition to this, that each of the four species indicates the aspect of unity,</t>
    <t s="56">behold, the mitzvah of taking the four species is to unite all four species,</t>
    <t s="57">which allude to the four categories within the Children of Israel,20</t>
    <t s="58">so that they all become one bundle to do Your will with a perfect heart.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="4">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that true and lasting unity of all types of Israel is achieved through teshuvah, which is above division and reaches the innermost essence of the soul, thereby making Israel like kings over all existence.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">4)</t>
    <t s="1">And behold, in order for the true unity</t>
    <t s="2">(and enduring)</t>
    <t s="3">of all four categories of Israel to be possible,</t>
    <t s="4">it is through teshuvah (repentance).</t>
    <t s="5">For, the concept of teshuvah is above division,</t>
    <t s="6">therefore it is "in one moment and in an instant."21</t>
    <t s="7">For this is the difference between the first tablets</t>
    <t s="8">(the concept of Torah as an intrinsic command)</t>
    <t s="9">and the second tablets</t>
    <t s="10">(the concept of Torah through teshuvah),</t>
    <t s="11">that in order to receive the first tablets, Moshe was on the mountain for forty days,</t>
    <t s="12">in addition to the preparation of "seven weeks you shall count" that preceded this.22</t>
    <t s="13">But not so with the second tablets,</t>
    <t s="14">behold, the forty days that Moshe was on the mountain were</t>
    <t s="15">(primarily)</t>
    <t s="16">in order to effect that the Holy One, blessed be He, would be appeased to Israel with joy and a full heart,23</t>
    <t s="17">and afterwards the tablets were given in one moment.</t>
    <t s="18">And behold, this concept</t>
    <t s="19">[that teshuvah is in one moment and in an instant]</t>
    <t s="20">emphasizes that the concept of teshuvah is above all measure and limitation,24</t>
    <t s="21">because true teshuvah reaches</t>
    <t s="22">(grasps)</t>
    <t s="23">the innerness and essence of the soul,</t>
    <t s="24">which is a level that is above division,</t>
    <t s="25">the aspect of "one"</t>
    <t s="26">(in one moment and in an instant)</t>
    <t s="27">of the soul.</t>
    <t s="28">And this is that which, through teshuvah, the unity of all the categories of Israel is effected,</t>
    <t s="29">from "your heads, your tribes" to "your hewers of wood and drawers of water,"</t>
    <t s="30">and in the manner of "you are standing this day, all of you," etc.,</t>
    <t s="31">"standing" (nitzavim) from the term "standing" (netzav)25</t>
    <t s="32">of a king,26</t>
    <t s="33">that Israel become kings and masters over the entire reality of the world,</t>
    <t s="34">beginning with this, that they are written and sealed for a good and sweet year, in the revealed and manifest good, even below ten handbreadths, also in physical matters,</t>
    <t s="35">since from the perspective of this level, it is not applicable to divide between spirituality and physicality, nor between above and below,</t>
    <t s="36">and this takes in (permeates) the entire order of the chain of descent (hishtalshelus) and also that which is above the order of the chain of descent.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="5">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that "one day they all came to greet the king their father" refers to Yom Kippur, the "one of the year," from which follows "let us all make one festival and rejoice with them," referring to Simchas Torah, also an aspect of "one."</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And this is the concept of "One day they all came to greet the king their father... let us all make one festival and rejoice with them,"</t>
    <t s="1">"One day"</t>
    <t s="2">(in which they all came to greet the king their father)</t>
    <t s="3">is Yom Kippur,</t>
    <t s="4">the "one" of the year</t>
    <t s="5">(and also the "one" of world and of soul),</t>
    <t s="6">and from this is drawn afterwards "let us all make one festival," etc., which refers to Simchas Torah,</t>
    <t s="7">which is also "one day"</t>
    <t s="8">(one festival),</t>
    <t s="9">the aspect of "one."</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
